idea: The design source for Artisign's own preview shell — the tool designing itself. Every token that has a counterpart in src/preview/style.css :root mirrors it by value AND by role name: the 19 colors (accent #2a3edb, canvas #e5e5e5, the grey text scale from text #1a1a1a down to text-faint #999), the six spacing steps xs4/sm6/md8/lg12/xl16/2xl24, radius.pill 999px and shadow.menu. Those can be compared line by line with the implementation, so a drift in either direction is visible rather than a matter of opinion. The typography scale and radius.sm/radius.md have no custom property behind them — they are design decisions, not a mirror, and should be read as such.

decisions.title: Tokens mirror the shipped stylesheet by value and by role name
decisions.body: Where a CSS custom property exists in src/preview/style.css, the token takes that property's role name and its exact value — never an appearance-based name, never a 'close enough' value re-derived by eye, and never an existing token whose name is convenient but whose value differs. Values with no custom property behind them (the 0.95rem rail icon, the 17px chip line-height) stay literal rather than inventing a token that implies a binding that does not exist. This is what makes the design checkable against the implementation instead of merely similar to it.

decisions.title: A component instance's own style is discarded — vary through variants
decisions.body: Writing <span class="$tag-chip" style="background: $color.accent"> does NOT tint that instance: the renderer emits the definition's root style and drops the instance's entirely. Confirmed by inspecting the rendered output, where the accent override was absent and only the definition's grey remained. Every visual difference between two instances therefore has to be a named variant. $tag-chip carries default / active / ref / badge for exactly this reason, and $btn carries default / confirm / confirm-disabled. The upside is that ad-hoc per-instance drift is impossible by construction; the cost is that a one-off tint needs a named variant and a reason to exist.

decisions.title: Component refs inside slot content are not resolved
decisions.body: A $component ref placed inside an instance's data-slot content survives into the output verbatim as class="$view-tab", unresolved, and the slot content's element ids are stripped as well — so such a node can be neither styled nor addressed by a flow or a comment. This ruled out the natural composition for the topbar (a tabs slot filled with $view-tab instances carrying their own flow targets). The topbar instead carries its tabs in the definition, with one variant per active tab, and the view-switching flows start from the sidebar's screen list, which are real, addressable nodes.

decisions.title: The filter field lives in the sidebar; the Board tab reports its result, it does not duplicate the input
decisions.body:
CHR-618/CHR-621: filter and pins are ephemeral per-project state in the daemon, one filter shared by the sidebar's screen list and the Board tab, and the Board shows filter matches ∪ pinned screens. Two ways to expose the shared filter on Board: (a) give the board toolbar its own input mirroring the sidebar's, or (b) keep the sidebar's existing field as the only input and have the board toolbar report the outcome. Chose (b). Reasoning: the sidebar's `screen-filter` input already exists and is exercised on every other tab; a second input box on the board would either drift from it or force a visibly-disabled duplicate. `$board-toolbar`'s `status` slot instead carries a plain-text summary. This means the Board tab keeps its sidebar expanded whenever the filter is non-empty and relevant — `board-view` renders the 280px expanded sidebar with its filter field for this reason. The other screens in this set keep the 36px collapsed rail since their point is the toolbar/canvas state, not the filter.

Also decided in this pass: the pinned/filter-match distinction reuses two existing pieces rather than a new component — `$pin-button`'s `pinned` variant (accent-filled) marks any pinned tile regardless of match, and `$board-tile`'s `outside-filter` variant (dashed accent border + a `$tag-chip` `badge`) labels a tile "pinned · outside filter" only when it is on the board solely because it is pinned. A tile that matches the filter needs no extra badge; a solid border communicates that on its own (`$board-tile` `default`).

Christian did not object to CTO review's other three recommendations, which are therefore also decided: the dashed-border-plus-badge treatment is the final pinned-outside-filter marker; the agent-presented banner stays visible until the human dismisses it; "Clear pins" requires no confirmation dialog.

decisions.title: Board zoom is a continuous 5%–200% slider on a viewport-shaped grid; low-zoom screens must be arithmetically honest (in mock terms); overview zoom hides the unpinned affordance
decisions.body:
Christian rejected the first CHR-621 pass for lacking a slider: a preset-only zoom group (Fit/50/100/200) cannot get far enough below 50% to make an overview of a large project (he named ~186 screens) usable. `$board-toolbar` now embeds `$zoom-slider` (−/+ step buttons, a 140px track, a live percentage readout), range **5%–200%**, linear. `Fit all` and `100%` are quick-jump buttons left of the slider; 50%/200% are not separate buttons any more now that the slider covers that range continuously.

SECOND CORRECTION: the first `board-view-zoomed-out` (42 tiles at 17% with "Fit all" active) still contradicted its own toolbar state — 42 tiles at 17% only fill a small corner of the canvas. Fixed by using Christian's actual project size (186 screens) and deriving the zoom from the resulting grid: with `$board-tile`'s native 180×150px footprint and the board's ~1356×764px usable canvas area, 186 tiles arrange as a 17×11 grid of 76×63px mini tiles — `76 ÷ 180 ≈ 42%`. `$board-toolbar`'s `fitall-edgesoff` variant and `$zoom-slider`'s `min` variant were updated in place to show 42%. This 42% is a mock-scale number — see the THIRD CORRECTION below for why the real number differs.

This also fixed the label-hiding threshold, previously a guessed "<20%": at 42% zoom, `typography.size-xs` (≈12.5px at 100%) scales to ≈5.2px, illegible, yet 42% sat inside the originally-declared 20–100% "truncated" band. Replaced the guess with a legibility-grounded threshold: labels hide entirely below ~60% (`8 ÷ 12.5 ≈ 64%`, the point the scaled font drops under a legible ~8px); 60–100% truncates with an ellipsis; 100%+ shows the full name.

THIRD CORRECTION (same day): once `board-view-zoomed-out` had 186 real tiles, the 181 unpinned `$pin-button` `default` markers turned into visual noise burying the 5 pinned ones — the only thing an overview zoom is actually for. Applied the same ~60% legibility threshold used for labels: below ~60% zoom, the unpinned pin affordance is not rendered at all (in the full app it becomes tile-hover-revealed instead, which a static screenshot cannot represent, so low-zoom reference screens simply omit it); the pinned (filled) marker always renders, at any zoom, since it conveys state a hover can't substitute for. `$board-tile`'s own `mini`-variant usage notes state this rule at the component level so it isn't re-litigated per screen.

FOURTH CORRECTION (implementation measurement, post-approval): two facts from the shipped/real implementation were folded back into this decision. (a) The board's tile grid is **viewport-shaped**, not a fixed layout: column/row count is computed from the current tile list and the board's actual surface area so Fit all makes best use of the viewport; recomputed on screen-list change, window resize, and project switch — never while the human is actively dragging the zoom slider. This design's screens still use a simplified fixed-size 180px mock tile in a fixed 1440×900 frame for illustration, not this real dynamic grid. (b) Real tiles are 390×844 (actual on-screen proportions), not this design's 180px mock — measured against Christian's real 186-screen project, the true fit-all scale came out to ~7.6%, well below this decision's original 10% floor, which would have clipped his own "show the whole project" requirement. The slider floor moved from 10% to 5% to leave headroom below the measured value. `board-view-zoomed-out`'s 42% remains in the design file as mock arithmetic — its own screen notes now say so explicitly and point back here; it is not the real number and was never meant to be, only a demonstration that a large project needs to go well below the old 50% preset floor.

Ctrl/Cmd+scroll-wheel over the canvas and pinch-to-zoom move the same slider value — not agent-settable, browser-local preference, same status as the edge toggle. Clicking `Fit all` computes whatever percentage fits every currently-shown tile (filter ∪ pins) into the viewport and sets the slider to that value once; it is not a sticky toggle.

Also in this pass: `$board-tile` was promoted (component, variants `default` / `outside-filter` / `mini`) once the tile card repeated a third time (`board-view`, `board-view-presented`, then 186× on `board-view-zoomed-out`) — see its own `usage` notes for the slot/variant breakdown and why `$pin-button` stays a sibling instance rather than a slot fill.

decisions.title: Follow mode: two new colors for read/write highlights, geometry stays inline, topbar-variant control is a design-file artefact, feed click exempt from pausing
decisions.body:
CHR-628/CHR-629 (ADR-005), APPROVED by Christian as designed. Three new tokens: `color.activity-read` (#0d9488, teal) and `color.activity-write` (#7c3aed, violet) for the two highlight kinds, plus `color.warning-subtle` (#fdf1e0) for the paused-toggle pill background. Read = solid 2px teal outline, appears immediately, fades 1.2s. Write = 2px DASHED violet outline plus a translucent `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)` wash, appears after the write's re-render or a 1s grace, fades 2.5s. Feed depth N=50. Both durations, N, and the token colors are approved, unchanged from the original proposal.

Inspect overlay and comment outlines, verified against shipped code (`artisign/src/preview/style.css` `#inspect-overlay`, `artisign/src/preview/comments.js:13-14`) rather than assumed: inspect overlay is accent blue, solid (`outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); background: rgba(42,62,219,0.06)`). Comment outlines are amber (`#d97706`) — the selected-target state is solid, but the comment-MARKER state is `outline: 2px dashed #d97706`, so dash pattern alone does not separate the write highlight from a dashed amber comment marker; the separation is hue plus the write highlight's translucent wash and (whole-screen case) its "Updated" badge, neither of which the pre-existing highlights carry. Under protanopia/deuteranopia (the common colorblind forms, blue-channel perception intact) violet's blue component should stay distinguishable from blue-absent amber even when hue-naming is unreliable; under full monochromacy the wash/badge are the only remaining cues — recorded honestly, not treated as fully solved.

The whole-screen write case (`write_html`, can't be localized to nodes) reuses the write violet at 3px around the whole screen frame plus a small "Updated" badge — chosen specifically to avoid reading as an error (no red, no exclamation glyph).

Geometry: highlights on the actual demo screens are inline token-styled positioning, not `$activity-highlight` component instances — that component is a fixed-size Design System reference only, because this project's components don't reliably accept per-instance width/height overrides and a highlight box has to match an arbitrary node's real bounding box. Same precedent as CHR-621's tile/pin geometry.

Follow toggle: the design file's `$topbar` `follow`/`follow-paused` variants are a DESIGN-FILE ARTEFACT, not the real implementation shape — confirmed by Christian: in the shipped app the follow toggle is ONE always-present topbar control (state-driven, not forked per tab), same as Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode already are. The two topbar variants exist here only because this project's components can't parameterize a slot-filled instance by external state, so two illustrative static variants were built to prove placement and both non-off appearances rather than one dynamic control.

CHANGED by Christian: clicking a feed entry does NOT pause follow, unlike every other human navigation (which still pauses per rule 1) and unlike an open comment/inspect mode (still pauses). A feed click is exempt because the human is still just watching the agent's own history, not designing something themselves — so the next navigating agent call pulls the view straight back to the agent's live target, no resume needed. Everything else in the pause/resume precedence (rule 2: Board presentation pauses; resume is always explicit, never automatic on condition-clear) is unchanged and approved.

A `component:`/`pattern:` navigation target highlights inside the Design System view's standalone render, same treatment — built as a new screen (`follow-highlight-definition`) rather than patching the shared `design-system-view` reference screen (a patch-then-revert happened during this work; verified unchanged via screenshot). A mockup target (no node ids) gets a transient column-level cue instead of a node box.

Feed: `$activity-entry` (variants `default`/`write`/`error`/`deleted`) and `$panel-tabs` (Elements/Activity header) let the feed live inside the existing right-side panel rather than adding a fifth 1440px-canvas column. Full interaction spec lives as tag notes on `chr-628`, not duplicated here.

component_usage.topbar:
The 48px application header, on every screen. Variants select which view tab reads as active — default (Screens) / design-system / board — plus empty, which is the pre-project state: title and a dashed project picker only. The canvas controls (zoom group, status-bar toggle) appear only on the default variant, matching the shipped app, where they are hidden outside the Screens view. Flow mode is pushed right with margin-left: auto; the topbar's own gap and padding are $spacing.xl (16px) — binding them to $spacing.md instead is the easy mistake, and it visibly squashes the bar.

CHR-628/CHR-629: two more variants, `follow` and `follow-paused`, added for the follow-mode toggle — each is a full copy of the `default` (Screens-tab) layout with a `$follow-toggle` instance (`following` / `paused` respectively) embedded directly in the definition, positioned right before the Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode cluster (margin-left: auto moved onto the toggle instead of `tb-flow`). These are additive — `default`/`design-system`/`board`/`empty` are byte-for-byte unchanged, so no existing screen using this component regressed. A production implementation would more likely parameterize follow state as a prop than fork variants per state × tab, but this project's components don't support that composition (a `$follow-toggle` instance can't be a slot fill either, per `no-component-refs-inside-slots`) — two illustrative variants were enough to prove placement and both non-off states without multiplying every tab × every follow-state combination.
component_usage.tag-chip: Neutral pill for a tag on a screen row, a design-system chip, or the 'project' badge in the folder browser — the shipped CSS makes .tag-chip and the badge pixel-identical, so one component covers both and no second badge style should be built. Single slot `label`. Variants: default (grey), active (accent fill, for the selected row's first tag), ref (monospace on surface, for a $token or $component reference), badge (accent-subtle). Wrap several in a flex row with gap $spacing.xs and margin-top $spacing.sm.
component_usage.btn: Dialog and empty-state action. default is the secondary/cancel treatment, confirm is the accent-filled primary, confirm-disabled is the same at 0.4 opacity for a form that is not yet satisfiable. Single slot `label`. Primary sits to the right of secondary in an actions row.
component_usage.quick-chip: Quick-access folder shortcut in the project dialogs (Home / Workspace / Desktop). The current variant marks the chip whose folder is being browsed. Single slot `label`.
component_usage.board-toolbar: Board-tab-only bar between the topbar and the canvas, 40px, same chrome tokens as topbar. Revised in the CHR-621 approval round: the zoom control is now a continuous `$zoom-slider` (10%–200%) rather than a fixed Fit/50/100/200 preset row — Christian's explicit requirement was that overviewing a large project (~190 screens) needs zoom well below any fixed preset. `Fit all` and `100%` stay as quick-jump buttons to the left of the slider (a vertical divider separates the two groups); 50%/100%/200% presets are dropped as separate buttons now that the slider covers that whole range continuously — only "Fit all" (fits every currently-shown tile) and "100%" (native scale) are common enough destinations to deserve a one-tap shortcut. Whichever quick-jump button matches the slider's current exact value gets the active (accent) treatment; neither is active if the slider sits at a value neither button represents. Edges toggle and the two slots (`status`, `actions`) are unchanged from before this revision — see git history / decision `chr621-filter-lives-in-sidebar` for that part. Variants: `default` (100% quick-jump active, edges on) for the standard working view, `fitall-edgesoff` (Fit all quick-jump active, slider near its floor, edges off) for a fully zoomed-out overview, `zoomedin` (slider at its ceiling, neither quick-jump active since 200% isn't one of the two shortcuts) for inspecting one screen closely.
component_usage.pin-button: Pin/unpin affordance, used in two places: fixed to a board tile's top-right corner, and inline at the end of a sidebar screen-list row. No slot — the icon is a static inline SVG map-pin glyph (`fill="currentColor"`, monochrome, 12px), not an emoji — the first version used an emoji pin glyph and CTO review flagged poor contrast on the accent fill plus inconsistent rendering across OSes; the SVG fixes both. `default` (grey outline, muted `currentColor` icon) is unpinned; `pinned` variant (accent fill, white `currentColor` icon) is pinned. The `pinned` variant doubles as the pinned marker itself — it stays visible on a tile regardless of whether that tile currently also matches the active filter, which is what makes a pinned-but-not-matching tile distinguishable from a plain filter match (which never carries this component in its filled state). Always render one instance per tile/row, in whichever state is correct (default or pinned) — an affordance that only appears on hover is not discoverable in a static design and untestable by screenshot; every tile and every visible sidebar row should show one, matching or not, pinned or not.
component_usage.zoom-slider: Continuous zoom control for the Board tab, embedded directly in `$board-toolbar` (not a slot fill — plain nested instance, resolves fine since it isn't inside another instance's `data-slot` content). −/+ step buttons flank a 140px track; the filled portion and thumb position communicate the current value, the `readout` slot holds the live percentage text. Range is **5%–200%**, linear: thumb position `= (value − 5) / 195 * 140px` from the track's left edge. 5% is the floor — CORRECTED from an initial 10% once implementation measured the real numbers: Christian's own requirement (CHR-621) was that Fit all must be able to show his whole ~186-screen project, and real tiles are 390×844 (not this design's 180px mock tiles), so the true fit-all scale on that project is ~7.6% — a 10% floor would have clipped it. Variants are illustrative fixed positions for the screens that need them, not a continuous range of variants: `default` (100%, thumb ~49% along the track), `min` (~15–20% in the mockup screens — see each screen's own notes for its actual illustrative value and remember the grid this design uses is a simplified fixed-size mock, not the viewport-shaped grid the real board uses), `max` (200%, thumb at the right end). A screen needing some other specific value should compute its own thumb/fill offsets with the same linear formula rather than approximate one of the three variants. Ctrl/Cmd+scroll-wheel and pinch-to-zoom on the canvas move this same value — this is a browser-local UI preference, not agent-settable, same as the rest of Board's zoom/edge state (see design-system decision `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` and the `chr-621` tag notes for the full state model, including how the real board's grid is computed).
component_usage.board-tile:
Board-tab tile card, promoted from inline markup once the same card shape appeared a third time (four tiles on `board-view`, three on `board-view-presented`, 186 on `board-view-zoomed-out` — the second-occurrence rule was already overdue). Slot `name` (plain text) holds the screen name; only `default` and `outside-filter` render it. `default` is a plain matching-or-unpinned tile (solid border, 180px wide, 120px thumb). `outside-filter` is the pinned-but-not-matching treatment (dashed accent border + a `$tag-chip` `badge` reading "pinned · outside filter") — use it only for a tile that is on the board solely because it is pinned, never for a tile that also matches the active filter. `mini` is the zoomed-out/fit-all form: no slot, no border-dash/badge distinction, no box-shadow-worthy detail — just a bordered block sized to the honest scale factor for that screen's zoom (see the `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` design-system decision for the arithmetic).

At `mini` scale, only ever place a `$pin-button` sibling on a tile that is actually pinned — do not render the unpinned (`default`) `$pin-button` at overview zoom. Below the same ~60% legibility threshold that hides tile-name labels, an unpinned pin affordance on every tile is pure visual noise that drowns the handful of pinned markers a human is actually scanning for; in the full-size app this affordance only appears on tile hover at low zoom (a static screenshot cannot show a hover state, so mini tiles here simply omit the unfilled marker rather than approximate hover). Pinned markers always render, at any zoom, since they carry information a hover can't substitute for.

The `$pin-button` marker is never nested inside this component (nesting a component ref inside another instance's slot fill does not resolve, per decision `no-component-refs-inside-slots`) — place `$pin-button` as a sibling of the `$board-tile` instance inside a shared `position: relative` wrapper div.
component_usage.follow-toggle: Per-browser preference toggle for follow mode (CHR-628/CHR-629), off by default. Three variants: `default` (off — grey outline, muted dot, label "Follow"), `following` (accent-filled, live accent dot, label "Following"), `paused` (`$color.warning`/`$color.warning-subtle` pill, label "Follow paused" plus a `Resume` action in accent text after a divider — clicking `Resume` re-arms follow and jumps to the latest target). Placed in the topbar's mode-button cluster, immediately before Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode — see `$topbar`'s `follow`/`follow-paused` variants, which embed this component directly in their own definition (not via a slot fill — nesting a component inside another instance's slot content does not resolve in this project, per decision `no-component-refs-inside-slots`; composing it directly inside `topbar`'s own template, the same way `$board-toolbar` embeds `$zoom-slider`, works fine). No slot: state is expressed entirely through the variant, there's nothing per-instance to fill.
component_usage.activity-highlight: Canonical style recipe for the two follow-mode highlight kinds (CHR-628/CHR-629), documented here at a fixed illustrative size for Design System reference and standalone screenshot — screens needing a highlight over an arbitrary node's actual bounding box do NOT instantiate this component (per-node geometry is dynamic and this project's components don't reliably take per-instance width/height overrides); instead they apply the same tokens (`$color.activity-read`, `$color.activity-write`, `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)`) directly, inline, positioned to the node in question — the same precedent already used for board-tile pin markers and canvas tile geometry elsewhere in this project. `default` (read): solid 2px `$color.activity-read` (teal) outline, appears immediately on a targeted read call (`get_screenshot`, `inspect_node`, `get_node`, `get_screen`, `get_mockup`), fades after 1.2s. `write`: 2px DASHED `$color.activity-write` (violet) outline plus a translucent `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)` fill wash — appears only after the write's re-render lands, or after a 1s grace if no re-render is observed, and fades after 2.5s. `write-screen`: the coarse whole-screen case after `write_html` (which the daemon can't localize to specific nodes) — a thicker 3px dashed `$color.activity-write` border around the entire screen frame plus a small pill badge reading "Updated" at the top-right corner, same 2.5s duration. The badge is what keeps this from reading as an error state (no red, no "!" glyph, positive-toned label) — see `follow-active-feed` for it applied to a real screen frame. Shape (dashed vs. solid) plus hue keeps read/write distinct from each other and from the existing inspect overlay (accent blue, in the Elements panel) and comment outline (assumed `$color.warning` amber per convention, not otherwise specified in this project) even for colorblind users. Both colors were checked against a dark screen background — see `follow-highlight-dark`.
component_usage.activity-entry: One row of the follow-mode activity feed (CHR-628/CHR-629), three slots: `tool` (mono, the MCP tool name), `target` (small muted line, e.g. "screen · checkout-cart" or "project-wide" for a broad read with no single target), `time` (relative timestamp, right-aligned). `default` = a read call: small circular dot in `$color.activity-read`. `write` = a write call: small SQUARE dot (same color family as the node highlight, shape difference kept for colorblind users) in `$color.activity-write`. `error` = a failed call (`ok:false`): red left border, tinted background, a small ✕ badge instead of a plain dot, tool name tinted `$color.error` — deliberately NOT styled identically to a normal row so a scanning eye catches it without reading the text; `cursor: default` (not `pointer`) since it never navigates. `deleted` = a call whose target no longer exists: whole row at 0.5 opacity, target slot replaced by a fixed "target removed" caption (do not fill the `target` slot on this variant, it's ignored), `cursor: default`. Both `error` and `deleted` are inert by design — CHR-629 decided disabled-look over a tooltip or toast for "this entry does nothing when clicked," consistent with how a disabled state reads everywhere else in this design system.
component_usage.panel-tabs: Small two-tab header for a side panel that now needs to switch between two bodies without spending another 280px column — built for the right-side panel's Elements/Activity split (CHR-628/CHR-629). `default` = Elements active (accent underline), Activity idle. `activity` = Activity active, Elements idle. No slot: exactly two fixed tabs, not a generic tab-bar primitive — promote a new variant (or a slotted generalization) only if a third tab is ever needed elsewhere; don't stretch this one to fit an unrelated case.
